text.p: Jimmy White, six times the beaten finalist, was knocked out 10-9 by fellow Englishman Anthony Hamilton in the first round of the world snooker championship on Wednesday night.

It was only the third first-round defeat for the popular White, 35, and it means he will drop out of the top 16 rankings next season for the first time in 15 seasons and will have to pre-qualify for this event.
White, who led 5-1 and 8-4 before Hamilton won six of the last seven frames, said he would battle to return to the event he has never won.

"I still love the game so there is no need for panic stations, though I will have to cut short my holidays this summer to play in the qualifying rounds. Hopefully I'll be back here again next year but I must be a certainty to draw Stephen Hendry in the first round."

Hamilton, 25 and world-ranked 22nd, immediately predicted White would be back. After compiling breaks of 96, 78, 76 and 72 on his way to victory, he said: "Jimmy is my hero. I took up the game because of him and he'll bounce straight back into the top 16 if he gets his nut (head) down."

Hamilton, the meets former champion John Parrott in the second round, added: "I think I played better than Jimmy, but his safety was 10 times better than mine. But this has to be the best win of my career considering who and where I was playing."

White called a foul on himself in the 17th frame after he feathered the cue ball with the colours at his mercy. In the final frame he led 35-1 but an inaccurate safety let Hamilton in for a winning break of 54.
World number two John Higgins survived the odd hiccup to ease his way past fellow Scot Graham Horne 10-6.

But it needed the help of a risky decision when he was 3-1 down to have a few inches sawn from his cue during the interval and he immediately made a break of 111. He also had the best break of the match, a 137.
He will meet the winner of a contest between Malta's Tony Drago and Welshman Dominic Dale, which Dale led 5-4 after the opening session.
